source.title: An algorithm for solving linear nonhomogeneous quaternion-valued differential equations and some open problems

accepted.question_text: For quaternion-valued differential equations, can one develop a theory of discontinuous systems that extends existing discontinuous control schemes—such as impulsive, switching, time-scale, piecewise, and fuzzy-system methods—to the quaternion-valued setting, and in particular determine whether discontinuous control strategies used for discontinuous ordinary differential equations can be adapted to discontinuous quaternion-valued differential equations?

evidence.quote: For the applications, it is known that several types of control schemes are proposed for the impulsive systems (e.g see [20, 25, 39]). Is it possible to extend such kinds of discontinuous control schemes to discontinuous QDEs?

accepted.question_text: What should a theory of fractional-order quaternion-valued differential equations look like, and how can one formulate and analyze fractional-order differential equations whose unknowns take values in the quaternion field?

evidence.quote: Fractional order differential equations have become a topic issue [36, 41]. So how about the fractional order quaternion-value differential equations? It is vacant in this field.

accepted.question_text: Can one develop a theory of soliton solutions for partial quaternion-valued differential equations, and in particular can the dynamical-systems method used to obtain solitons of partial differential equations be extended to produce soliton solutions in the quaternion-valued setting?

evidence.quote: And how about the Soliton solutions of partial quaternion-value differential equations? In particular, it is known that the dynamic system method is a powerful tool to obtain the solitons of PDEs [19, 38]. Does the dynamic system method can be extended to the solitons of partial quaternion-value differential equations? It is open.

accepted.question_text: When quaternion-valued differential equations are augmented with reaction-diffusion terms to account for spatial variation, what kinds of dynamics can occur, including phenomena analogous to the spatiotemporal patterns and instabilities known for reaction-diffusion systems in mathematical biology and related applications?

evidence.quote: In particular, in mathematical biology, when the spatial variation is also taken into account, the population system (ordinary differential equations) can be described by a system of reaction-diffusion equations. For examples, Turing instability and spatiotemporal patterns in chemical reactions and ecological systems have been reported [28]. What kinds of dynamics can exhibit for QDEs with reaction-diffusion? It is unknown.

accepted.question_text: Can a bifurcation theory for quaternion-valued differential equations be developed for systems subjected to perturbations, and in particular how should an appropriate Poincare map be defined in the quaternion-valued setting so that bifurcation phenomena can be studied rigorously?

evidence.quote: For QDEs, I guess that the bifurcations can occur if it is subjected to some perturbations. The difficulty is how to define the Poincar´e map? This is challenging.

accepted.question_text: How do time delays affect quaternion-valued differential equations, including whether delay can change stability or generate bifurcation and chaotic behavior in quaternion-valued systems, as happens in some delayed ordinary differential equations?

evidence.quote: In real world applications, delay may drive the stability switch or not. Sometimes, bifurcations and chaos occur due to the delay (e.g. see[14, 29]). So does the delay affect the quaternion differential equations? It is open.

accepted.question_text: Can one formulate and study fuzzy quaternion differential equations that provide a mathematical model for quaternion-valued dynamical systems with uncertainty or ambiguity, analogous to the role played by fuzzy differential equations in other real-world modeling problems?

evidence.quote: As we know, the study of fuzzy differential equations provides a suitable environment for mathematical modeling of real-world problems involving uncertainty or ambiguity [3]. Therefore, investigating the fuzzy quaternion differential equations will be an interesting topic.

accepted.question_text: Which real-world phenomena can be effectively modeled and analyzed using quaternion-valued differential equations, and how should the associated quaternion-valued optimization and application theory be developed in areas such as engineering control, color recognition, color image compression, and robotic systems control, where quaternion-valued methods may carry richer information than real-valued models?

evidence.quote: Real world applications of QDEs: Many questions on the theory of QDEs still remain open, not mention to the practical applications of QDEs to study the real world phenomenon.

Thus, the quaternion-valued optimization is an interesting topic and arises in a broad variety of applications and engineering control, color recognition, color image compression, robotic systems control and so on.
However, this is only the beginning. The work should be on going in the field of the quaternion-valued optimization.

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record to the publisher PDF for DOI 10.3934/dcdss.2021162 and mapped Section 5 on pages 10-11 as the open-problem region.
Extracted the eight numbered open-problem items listed in Section 5, 'Discussion and some open problems'.
Expanded the discontinuous-QDE item into a standalone question while preserving the paper's control-scheme framing.
Rewrote the fractional-order item as a self-contained question about building a theory of fractional-order quaternion-valued differential equations.
Expanded the soliton item to state both the target equations and the dynamic-systems method mentioned in the source.
Made the reaction-diffusion item self-contained by inlining the spatial-variation motivation and the target dynamics question.
Rewrote the bifurcation item around the explicit obstacle identified in the source: defining a Poincare map for QDEs.
Expanded the delay item into a standalone question about stability, bifurcation, and chaos under delay.
Converted the implicit fuzzy-QDE research direction into a standalone modeling question without adding unsupported technical claims.
Combined the explicit applications item and its continuation on quaternion-valued optimization into one self-contained applications question.
Kept all eight numbered items as distinct questions because they address different problem domains.
Accepted items have page-grounded evidence and self-contained rewrites without unresolved cross-references; no metadata-only extraction was used.
